angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 13,518,842 km at 56.31 pc = 3.21 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 57399: distance 56.306 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.009), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 56.306 +/- 0.507 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 16.4382 +/- 0.1130 mas (same row, RUWE 2.15), 145.5 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 19.432 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 57399: radius 19.432 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 136.908 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.057) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 13,518,842 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4482 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 57399: effective temperature 4482 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.06) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 57399: effective temperature 4482 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.06) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)
spectralTypeSource: SIMBAD, * chi UMa: spectral type K0.5IIIb: (1989ApJS...71..245K)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, * chi UMa: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
projectedRotationSpeedSource: SIMBAD, * chi UMa: projected rotation speed 2.3 km/s, the measurement SIMBAD prefers (2008AJ....135..209M)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 605) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.

surfaceGravitySource: log g 1.86 from 2021MNRAS.505.4496G; the 19 published values span log g 1.15 to 2.35, across which the limb law changes by at most 0.4% of the centre brightness (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.505.4496G)
